subject: Threat surface audit: vendor selection and coverage gaps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Threat surface audit vendor shortlist and coverage criteria

Marcus/Laura —

Per our compliance calendar we need to lock the vendor for the annual offensive engagement (red team + targeted application tests) before EoY. I ran procurement's minimums and compiled a shortlist: WhiteHat Security and VectorSec. Attachment: vendor_shortlist_scorecard.xlsx.

A couple of things I'd like us to confirm this week:
- Minimum deliverables: exploit walkthroughs, prioritized remediation list, retest window (30 days), and executive summary for SLT.
- Coverage: external infra, web apps, auth flows, and an optional mobile assessment add-on.
- Requirements: SOC2 Type II, background checks for testers, explicit non-disclosure / rules of engagement language, and ability to do limited source-code review or instrumentation.

Can you take a look at the scorecard and flag any must-have items that would disqualify a vendor? I know budget is tight — I want to balance depth vs cost.

Thanks,
Naomi
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vendor_shortlist_scorecard.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Threat surface audit vendor shortlist and coverage criteria

Thanks Naomi — quick notes:

- Add a clause for test-data handling and retention (we need logs retained for 90 days post-engagement).
- Ensure SLAs for escalations during active findings (30-minute response for critical issues during engagement window).
- For technical scope, prefer a vendor with both red-team capability and dedicated appsec engineers who can do limited SCA and code review; that will reduce back-and-forth on exploitability.

Looping in Marissa for procurement cadence — Marissa, can procurement handle a PO + SOW combo with a 30-day invoice term? Also ask Legal to fast-track the ROE (I will escalate if needed).

I'll review the scorecard and add budget thresholds by EOD.

Cheers,
Marcus
Director, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Hayes <oliver@whitehatsec.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: WhiteHat: proposed engagement summary and scope highlights

Marcus/Naomi —

Thanks for the invite to bid — attached is our proposal (whitehat_proposal_v3.pdf). Quick summary:
- 8–10 tester red team engagement over 7 calendar days (3 targeted external windows + 2 days full-scope app testing)
- Deliverables: technical report with PoC, prioritized remediation matrix, executive summary, and one workshop for engineering (2 hours)
- Optional: source-code review day for two critical services (add-on)
- SLA: 24-hour triage for critical findings during active testing window; background checks and SOC 2 attestation available on request

We can accommodate your 30-day retest requirement and provide a dedicated account lead for communications. I can also share a redacted sample report if that helps.

Attachment: whitehat_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal stub)

—Oliver
Oliver Hayes
Engagement Lead, WhiteHat Security
oliver@whitehatsec.com
+1 415 555 0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Threat surface audit vendor shortlist and coverage criteria

Quick gap analysis after reading WhiteHat's proposal + VectorSec's scope notes (attached). Highlights from the scorecard:

- WhiteHat scores higher on red-team depth and exploit craftsmanship but is ~12% above our preferred budget threshold.
- VectorSec is more prescriptive on source-code review and supply-chain checks; they offer a longer retest window as part of their standard package.
- Both vendors meet SOC2 and can provide tester background checks.

I've attached vendor_shortlist_scorecard.xlsx with my scoring notes and vectorsec_scope_notes.docx. If budget is the primary constraint we can negotiate deliverable granularity (e.g., limit source-code review to a single service, reduce on-site days).

Laura
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vendor_shortlist_scorecard.xlsx, vectorsec_scope_notes.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Threat surface audit vendor shortlist and coverage criteria

Thanks — Laura this is helpful.

Procurement constraints: we have budget authority up to $85k for this engagement in Q4 without a finance exception. WhiteHat's ask (as-written) is $96k. Two options:
1) Ask WhiteHat for a reduced scope (remove source-code review, compress on-site days) and push for $80–85k.
2) Accept WhiteHat at $96k and request a one-time finance approval (I will need SLT sign-off).

Negotiation points for me to raise with vendors: insurance limits, tester background check evidence, explicit post-engagement retest and SLA, and a clause about not publishing raw exploit code outside remediation reports.

Marissa — can you confirm PO timeline and whether we can do PO+SOW by Dec 6? If not, I'll escalate to Finance.

Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver@whitehatsec.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final vendor recommendation and next steps

Team —

Procurement has reviewed both proposals and confirmed we can issue a PO+SOW. Given the risk profile and exec preference for demonstrated exploitability, recommendation is to proceed with WhiteHat with the following negotiated exceptions:
- Remove optional full source-code day; include a targeted code instrument review for two critical services only (saves ~12k).
- 30-day retest retained; 24-hour triage negotiated to 12-hour for critical findings during active window.
- WhiteHat to provide insurance certificate and background-check evidence prior to start.

I've initiated the PO and uploaded the docusign envelope for the SOW: https://www.docusign.com/Sign?env=prod&acct=ABCD1234. Once signed, procurement will issue PO-2026-REDTEAM-1129 and target start date is Jan 10, 2027.

Attachments included: whitehat_proposal_v3.pdf, vendor_shortlist_scorecard.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: whitehat_proposal_v3.pdf, vendor_shortlist_scorecard.xlsx
